newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst eyes lower tax rate in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst eyes lower tax rate in 1997.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs giant Hoechst AG said on Monday that it expected to show a lower tax rate for the 1997 business year, as special factors which pushed the rate up last year had been digested.

"Our tax rate for the first quarter 1997 was 44 percent as compared with 45 percent for the first quarter 1996, and we hope to decrease this further," Hoechst chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schmieder told a conference call after the group announced first quarter results.
Schmieder explained that the full year tax rate for 1996 stood at 47 percent, a particularly high number due to the heavy taxation on the sale of the SGL Carbon AG unit.
Asked whether Schmieder expected the full year tax rate for 1997 to be below the first quarter rate, he said, "that is the assumption at this moment, but we can't commit to this."
